title: 153 The linear relationship of forage intake, residual feed intake, and greenhouse gas emissions between lactation and gestation in beef cows
content:
Abstract
The objective of this study was to determine the linear relationship of dry matter intake (DMI), residual feed intake (RFI), and greenhouse gas emissions among stages of production in mature beef cows fed an unprocessed grass hay diet. Forty-one mature Angus and Angus-cross cows were used in a 100-d, early-mid lactation experiment (LACT) followed by a 89-d, early-mid gestation experiment (GEST). Cows were housed in drylot pens at the Oklahoma State University Range Cow Research Center. Each pen was equipped with individual intake monitoring systems (C-Lock Inc, Rapid City, SD) with a stocking rate of 2.6 cows per feeder. Cows were offered ad libitum access to long-stem, unprocessed bermudagrass hay (LACT = 12.6% CP and 57% TDN, GEST = 12.4% CP and 54% TDN) and a mineral/vitamin supplement. An open-circuit, portable gas quantification system (GreenFeed, C-Lock Inc., Rapid City, SD) was rotated through pens to measure CO2, CH4, and O2 flux. Mid-test metabolic body weight (MBW), average daily gain (ADG), average milk yield, and age accounted for 62.9% and 48.0% of the variation in forage dry matter intake for LACT and GEST respectively. Cows were classified by k-means clustering into three categories of forage utilization efficiency based on RFI of efficient (n = 14 LACT, n = 15 GEST), moderate (n = 18 LACT, n = 13 GEST), and inefficient (n = 9 LACT, n = 10 GEST). LACT DMI means for the efficient, moderate, and inefficient groups were 13.4, 14.3, and 16.6 kg, and GEST DMI means for the 3 groups were 11.7, 12.1 and 16.0 kg respectively (P ≤ 0.01). Efficient classified cows consumed 20.5% (LACT) and 31.2% (GEST) less hay than inefficient classified cows (P ≤ 0.01). There were no significant differences for MBW, ADG, milk yield, milk energy concentration, body condition score (BCS), CO2, CH4, or O2 between classification groups in either physiological stage. There were strong (P ≤ 0.01) positive phenotypic correlations for DMI (r = 0.86) and RFI (r = 0.75) between the two physiological stages. Between LACT and GEST, 11 cows changed efficiency status by one classification group, and 1 cow changed efficiency status by two classification groups. In addition, there were strong positive phenotypic correlations between DMI and CO2 or CH4 during LACT (r = 0.61 CO2 and r = 0.61 CH4) and GEST (r = 0.59 CO2 and r = 0.56 CH4). The results from this study suggest that long-stem, unprocessed hay intake and utilization efficiency in mature beef cows is correlated across lactation and gestation with minimal re-ranking.
